newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE futures rise now looking short term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE futures rise now looking short term.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

* $19 should now be sustainable and possibly a test of the recent $19.64 high may even be seen. * In the next week or so the market should break back down to test the $18.45 low and possibly the $17.89 low of June 20.
IPE Brent crude and gas oil prices should continue their slow trek higher with both markets having held support and pulled off the lows on Monday, analysts said.

However analyst views were mixed over how long the upside could be sustained with some expecting the market to return to its overall downtrend seen since the beginning of the year in the not to distant future.

October Brent opened and closed below trendline support on Monday, but analysts remained positive, short term, with the price action pegging the bulk of trade near the top of the day's trading range and the contract ending 22 cents off the lows on a late rally.
Steve Kwan, analyst at MMS in London said "$19 should now be sustainable and possibly a test of the recent $19.64 high (August 4) may be seen".
"Momentum is good and a break out of the recent congested range between $18 and $19 puts a good base in the market giving room for a rally to $20," he added.

Monday's price action left a hammer formation on the spot month continuation chart which according to Japanese candlestick charting techniques coming in the downtrend of the past three-days could flag a return to higher ground, or at least it puts a good base in the market at around $18.90-95.
Nicholas Wilson, analyst at MeesPierson Isle of Man said: "This pattern and the similar one, though not so good for gas oil, could support a recovery for a short while.

He expected the market to test $19.40 and possible even $19.61 where, on the October chart, an imperfect double top lies between the highs of August 4 and 5 which could provide stiff resistance and he said any gains would be short term.
"In the next week or so the market should break back down to test the $18.45 low (August 8) and possibly the $17.89 low of June 20", Wilson said.
He explained the bearish sentiment stems from the beginning of the year since when the market has been moving progressively lower.
"The uptrend was fractured and the backwardation disappeared around April/May/June," Wilson said.

A series of parallel trendlines drawn from the October contract peak of $20.61 in January and the subsequent peaks throughout the year also appears to back up this theory with the market ending in a deeper trough after each rally faltered.

Moving averages continue to offer support. The 10 and 20-day measures are on a path of convergence that crosses around 60 percent, a level which could turn the market either way though with the market still managing to hold above the longer term 20-day average analysts say the direction is likely to be higher.

Historic volatility measures are fairly low with the 10 and 20-day measures hovering around 20 percent and Brent still has plenty of room to move higher short term with the 14-day RSI stuck in neutral territory around 50 percent.

Gas oil showed a similar pattern of trade on Monday dipping and stay below short term support stemming from the August 11 low of $167.50 though the contract remains well above longer term uptrend support from the June 20 low of $158.

Moving averages are also supportive though there is little sign of a direction giving convergence though a similar Japanese hammer pattern to that of Brent may be flagging at least an end to the recent downtrend.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
